clue.text: Area of Ireland in which real kid is processed

indicators.note: processed means worked over and changed, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Ireland a genuine young goat is being handled at a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is processed' rearranges REALKID into the county name; KILDARE is a county west of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is an Irish county, a region of the island.

clue.text: Cur, say, with Sarah going round a reception room at the spa

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, keeping its sound but not its spelling

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, its sound written here with K

indicators.note: going round means encircling the following letter

parts.note: Sal is a familiar form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A mongrel goes with a woman around a spa lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts A inside SAL to give SAAL after KUR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A kursaal is a public hall for visitors at a German health resort.

clue.text: Similar to meaty chunks perhaps, dressed up

explanation.surface: Something looks like pet food and is overdressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally resembling a pet's meal, and idiomatically flashy and over-smart in dress.

clue.text: Useful cockney fellow

indicators.note: Cockneys drop the initial aitch, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: handy means useful

explanation.surface: A London man who is helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a man's name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: Give a subject a title perhaps

definitions.text: Give a subject a title perhaps

parts.words: Give a subject a title perhaps
parts.note: reads like naming an essay topic, but means raising one of the monarch's subjects to the peerage

explanation.surface: Name a theme for an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to make someone a noble, as a peer.

clue.text: An Italian writer of music played rather slowly

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Florentine poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian author composed music that is performed at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian writer' looks like the subject, but it simply supplies DANTE after AN; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An andante is a movement or passage marked to be performed at a moderate walking tempo.

clue.text: Mad dash for a place in Kent

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A frantic rush to a town in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges DASHFOR. Kent is a county in south-east England, and Ashford a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashford is a Kentish market town.

clue.text: Empty out onto the rubbish heap

explanation.surface: Tipping out onto the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump is to tip out, and a dump is a tip for refuse.

clue.text: Keeping out of trouble? That's the policy

definitions.text: Keeping out of trouble? That's the policy

parts.words: Keeping out of trouble? That's the policy
parts.note: suggests a person staying out of mischief, but describes a state declining to involve itself in others' conflicts

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stay out of mischief as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's stance of not interfering in other countries' affairs.

clue.text: Delightful city is an absurdity

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: an absurdity is nonsense, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Saying a pleasant city is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurdity' rearranges ISAN into SIAN after ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian means blissful, as of the Elysian Fields of the blessed.

clue.text: Was successful as a croupier

explanation.surface: A gambler had a good night, like the casino dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake in the money is idiom for earning a lot, and literally what a croupier does with a rake gathering chips.

clue.text: Fixture not found at home

explanation.surface: A football match played on the other side's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An away game is a fixture played on the opponents' ground, and someone away is absent from their house.

clue.text: Detest coming from harbour leaving ancient city behind

indicators.note: the answer's letters are made out of those of the word harbour, rearranged

parts.note: Ur was the ancient Sumerian city of Abraham

explanation.surface: Hating to arrive from port after quitting an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving ... behind' says UR is dropped from HARBOUR; the remaining HARBO, 'coming from' it, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe it, a strong synonym.

clue.text: One who is not in favour ain't troubled

definitions.text: One who is not in favour

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the contraction are stirred up

explanation.surface: A colloquial negative feels upset at an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the four letters of AIN'T, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is an opponent, someone against a proposal.

clue.text: A tax popular with racegoers!

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A levy that pleases fans of horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the place: Ascot is the racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous racecourse much frequented by race fans.

clue.text: Unevenly?

parts.note: reads as irregularly, but the cryptic sense is in a manner that is not even, like the numbers 1, 3, 5

explanation.definitionFit: Odd numbers are those not even, so strangely is also in a not-even way.

clue.text: Seek loo out for inspection

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for the toilet takes a quick look around.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is informal for a quick look or check.

clue.text: Resentment at counterfeit gone astray

parts.note: a dud is a fake, such as a forged note

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of gone are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that fake money has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' turns GONE into GEON after DUD; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is deep indignation, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Fail to get experience when the young lady is 10

parts.note: Miss is the title for an unmarried girl
10 across is AWAY, and away means out, not at home

explanation.surface: A girl's absence means she misses something.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '10' points to 10 across, AWAY, which here stands for OUT; 'when' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss out is to lose the chance of enjoying something.

clue.text: Ran the way the director did?

explanation.surface: Someone ran the company as its boss would.
explanation.definitionFit: Managed means ran, and a director managed the business.

clue.text: It was permitted after biting small pie

indicators.note: after puts the permission word behind the sharp one

parts.note: tart means sharp-tasting, biting
let is the past tense of let, allowed

explanation.surface: Someone was allowed to bite into a little pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' looks like the action, but it supplies TART.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartlet is a little open pastry, a small tart.

clue.text: Finished everywhere

explanation.surface: Something is done and spread throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: All over means at an end, and also in every place.

clue.text: Doomed dogs trapped by wild cat going round

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the next pieces
wild means uncontrolled, so the letters of cat are rearranged

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs

explanation.surface: Hounds caught by a savage feline are done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns CAT into ACT, which 'going round' and 'trapped by' put about CURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurst is an old form of accursed, under a curse.

clue.text: In which things are taken the wrong way

definitions.text: In which things are taken the wrong way

parts.words: In which things are taken the wrong way
parts.note: sounds like a misunderstanding, but describes property seized unlawfully

explanation.surface: A misunderstanding where remarks are misinterpreted.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft by force, taking goods illegally.

clue.text: Not applicable, provided it is artless

parts.note: N/A is the form abbreviation for not applicable
provided means on condition that, which is if

explanation.surface: A form entry marked irrelevant shows simplicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif means naive and unsophisticated, an innocent lack of guile.

clue.text: Couple getting support

explanation.surface: Two people find backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, as of game birds, and a prop or strut.

clue.text: Small bolt NB is replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A note about a little fastener being changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' looks like S, but it belongs to the definition; 'replaced' rearranges NBIS. A snib is a Scottish word for a door catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snib is a little catch or latch on a door or window.

clue.text: Dry up after a song

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the A
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: A singer's voice fails after one number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIR into RIA; 'after' puts it behind A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo piece in an opera.

clue.text: Form of worship I pore over

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study closely

explanation.surface: Someone studies a religious practice.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image venerated in Orthodox churches, an object of devotion.

clue.text: The usual habit of a doctor?

definitions.text: The usual habit of a doctor?

parts.words: The usual habit of a doctor?
parts.note: read as the custom most commonly followed, then as the line of work of a family physician

explanation.surface: What a doctor routinely does.
explanation.definitionFit: General practice is common procedure, and also the work of a family doctor.

clue.text: In the corridor, man there who is not very active

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sleepy man is standing in the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive, as a sleeping volcano.

clue.text: Accommodation for Mr Lawrence at French town

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, known by his initials
Nancy is a city in Lorraine

explanation.surface: Lodgings for Lawrence of Arabia in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of rented premises, a lease on a home.
